---
name: qwen35-windows-attention-pitfall
description: Qwen3.5 training on Windows OOMs at long context — float attention mask forces a (heads,T,T) fp32 grad buffer in SDPA backward
metadata:
  type: reference
---

Qwen3.5 (qwen3_5, transformers 5.8) builds an explicit float attention mask even for text-only inputs (to support image-token regions). Torch mem-efficient SDPA backward then allocates a (heads, T, T) fp32 grad-bias buffer — 9.77 GiB at T=12.8k on Qwen3.5-4B — and flash SDP rejects head_dim 256. On Windows this spills into shared memory ("42 GiB allocated" on a 16 GB card) before OOM.

**Why:** the mask is plain causal for text-only batches, so materializing it is pure waste.

**How to apply:** use `sdft/patches.py` (`attn_implementation: sdpa_textonly` in the config) which registers an AttentionInterface entry passing `is_causal=query_len>1` and mask=None. Text-only batches ONLY — wrong for image inputs. Also: GDN layers fall back to a slow torch path unless flash-linear-attention (installed, fla 0.5.0) AND causal-conv1d (not installed; CUDA ext, hard to build on Windows) are both present — WSL2 is the clean fix for full speed.
